/**
 * This version is stamped on May 10, 2016
 *
 * Contact:
 *   Louis-Noel Pouchet <pouchet.ohio-state.edu>
 *   Tomofumi Yuki <tomofumi.yuki.fr>

/* gemver.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "gemver.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE *alpha,
		 DATA_TYPE *beta,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(u1,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(v1,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(u2,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(v2,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(w,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(z,N,n))
{
  int i, j;

  *alpha = 1.5;
  *beta = 1.2;

  DATA_TYPE fn = (DATA_TYPE)n;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      u1[i] = i;
      u2[i] = ((i+1)/fn)/2.0;
      v1[i] = ((i+1)/fn)/4.0;
      v2[i] = ((i+1)/fn)/6.0;
      y[i] = ((i+1)/fn)/8.0;
      z[i] = ((i+1)/fn)/9.0;
      x[i] = 0.0;
      w[i] = 0.0;
      for (j = 0; j < n; j++)
        A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*j % n) / n;
    }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(w,N,n))
{
  int i;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("w");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, w[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("w");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_gemver[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
		   DATA_TYPE alpha,
		   DATA_TYPE beta,
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(u1,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(v1,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(u2,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(v2,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(w,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(z,N,n))
{
  int i, j;

#pragma scop

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++)
      A[i][j] = A[i][j] + u1[i] * v1[j] + u2[i] * v2[j];

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++)
      x[i] = x[i] + beta * A[j][i] * y[j];

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    x[i] = x[i] + z[i];

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++)
      w[i] = w[i] +  alpha * A[i][j] * x[j];

#pragma endscop
}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  DATA_TYPE alpha;
  DATA_TYPE beta;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(u1, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(v1, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(u2, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(v2, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(w, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(x, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(y, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(z, DATA_TYPE, N, n);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, &alpha, &beta,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u1),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(v1),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u2),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(v2),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(w),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(z));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_gemver (n, alpha, beta,
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u1),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(v1),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u2),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(v2),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(w),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(z));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(w)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(u1);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(v1);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(u2);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(v2);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(w);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(x);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(y);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(z);

  return 0;
}

# Optimized polyhedral-style model for gemver

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # Dense matrix A, row-major
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Input / inout vectors, contiguous
    u1[i]: in    DATA_TYPE = i
    v1[j]: in    DATA_TYPE = j
    u2[i]: in    DATA_TYPE = i
    v2[j]: in    DATA_TYPE = j
    y[i]:  in    DATA_TYPE = i
    z[i]:  in    DATA_TYPE = i
    x[i]:  inout DATA_TYPE = i
    w[i]:  inout DATA_TYPE = i

    # Temporaries to reduce arithmetic and improve reuse
    # y_beta[j] = beta * y[j], reused across all i in x-update
    y_beta[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = j
    # x_alpha[j] = alpha * x[j], reused across all i in w-update
    x_alpha[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = j

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE
    # Tunable blocking and vectorization parameters
    TI: int  # tile size for i
    TJ: int  # tile size for j
    VEC: int # SIMD width in elements (e.g., 4 or 8)

computation:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1) Rank-2 update:
    #    A <- A + u1 * v1^T + u2 * v2^T
    #    Matches:
    #      for i
    #        for j
    #          A[i][j] += u1[i]*v1[j] + u2[i]*v2[j];
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    A_UPDATE:
      for i, j:
        A[i, j] = A[i, j]
                  + u1[i] * v1[j]
                  + u2[i] * v2[j]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2a) Precompute beta-scaled y to avoid recomputing beta*y[j]
    #     in the matrix–vector product.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    Y_SCALE:
      for j in [0, N):
        y_beta[j] = beta * y[j]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2b) x <- x + beta * A^T * y
    #     Implemented as:
    #       x[i] = x[i] + sum_j A[j, i] * y_beta[j]
    #     Matches:
    #       for i
    #         for j
    #           x[i] += beta * A[j][i] * y[j];
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    X_UPDATE:
      for i in [0, N):
        x[i] = x[i] + sum(j in [0, N), A[j, i] * y_beta[j])

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3) x <- x + z   and   x_alpha <- alpha * x
    #    We fuse the add and scale so alpha*x[j] is computed once and
    #    reused in the next matrix–vector product.
    #    Matches:
    #      for i
    #        x[i] += z[i];
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    X_ADD_Z_AND_SCALE:
      for i in [0, N):
        x[i]      = x[i] + z[i]
        x_alpha[i] = alpha * x[i]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4) w <- w + alpha * A * x
    #    Implemented as:
    #      w[i] = w[i] + sum_j A[i, j] * x_alpha[j]
    #    Matches:
    #      for i
    #        for j
    #          w[i] += alpha * A[i][j] * x[j];
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    W_UPDATE:
      for i in [0, N):
        w[i] = w[i] + sum(j in [0, N), A[i, j] * x_alpha[j])

dependencies:
    # Global phase ordering (barriers between phases)
    A_UPDATE -> Y_SCALE -> X_UPDATE -> X_ADD_Z_AND_SCALE -> W_UPDATE

optimization:
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # General notes:
    # - A is row-major. Loops that iterate j as the innermost index
    #   over A[i, j] benefit from unit-stride accesses.
    # - y_beta and x_alpha eliminate one multiplication per A-access
    #   in X_UPDATE and W_UPDATE, cutting total multiplications from
    #   ~6 N^2 to ~4 N^2.
    # - Parallelization is across i (or i-tiles), since updates to
    #   distinct elements of x[i] and w[i] are independent.
    # --------------------------------------------------------------

    # ---------------- A_UPDATE: rank-2 update of A -----------------
    # Tile the i and j loops so that an A tile plus the needed u/v
    # slices fit in cache.
    block(i, I_A, TI)
    block(j, J_A, TJ)
    hoist(I_A)              # make tile loops outermost

    # Parallelize across i-tiles; each tile writes disjoint rows of A.
    parallelize(I_A)

    # Vectorize inner j over contiguous A[i, j], v1[j], v2[j].
    vectorize(j, VEC)

    # Optionally hoist row-invariant u1[i], u2[i] into registers
    hoist(i)   # keep u1[i], u2[i] in registers within the inner j-loop

    # ------------- X_UPDATE: x += A^T * (beta y) ------------------
    # Access pattern A[j, i] is column-wise in the naive loop nest;
    # to make it row-major, we compute the reduction sum over j using
    # a j-outer, i-inner implementation within tiles.
    #
    # Mathematically:
    #   x[i] = x[i] + sum_j A[j, i] * y_beta[j]
    # allows reordering of (i, j) iteration as long as the sum over j
    # for each x[i] is preserved.

    block(j, J_X, TJ)       # tile over rows of A
    block(i, I_X, TI)       # tile over columns of A
    interchange(i, j)       # implement tiles as:
                            #   for J_X
                            #     for I_X
                            #       for j in tile J_X
                            #         for i in tile I_X:
                            #           x[i] += A[j, i] * y_beta[j]

    # Parallelize across I_X tiles: each x[i] is updated independently.
    parallelize(I_X)

    # Vectorize across i inside a fixed row j to exploit unit-stride
    # accesses to A[j, i] and x[i].
    vectorize(i, VEC)

    # ------------- X_ADD_Z_AND_SCALE: x += z; x_alpha = alpha*x ---
    # Simple 1D loop; trivially parallel and vectorizable.
    parallelize(i)
    vectorize(i, VEC)

    # ------------- W_UPDATE: w += A * (alpha x) -------------------
    # Standard GEMV with row-major A: i-outer, j-inner is already
    # cache-friendly and vectorizable.

    block(i, I_W, TI)
    block(j, J_W, TJ)
    hoist(I_W)              # outer tile in i

    # Parallelize across I_W tiles: each tile updates disjoint w[i].
    parallelize(I_W)

    # Vectorize across inner j over contiguous A[i, j], x_alpha[j].
    vectorize(j, VEC)

    # ----------------- Optional higher-level tweak ----------------
    # fuse(A_UPDATE, X_UPDATE):
    #   # Conceptual directive (not standard):
    #   # Evaluate A_UPDATE and X_UPDATE in a single (i, j) traversal:
    #   #   - First update A[i, j] using u1[i], v1[j], u2[i], v2[j].
    #   #   - Immediately accumulate into x[j] using y_beta[i] and the
    #   #     updated A[i, j]:
    #   #       x[j] += A[i, j] * y_beta[i]
    #   # This preserves x = x + beta * A^T * y mathematically while
    #   # reducing A traffic from two passes (update, then A^T*y) to one.
--- END OF MODEL: gemver-01 ---

--- START OF MODEL: gemver-02 ---
domain:
    # Problem size (square matrix)
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # Matrix A is stored row-major: A[i, j] at offset i * N + j
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Input vectors (read-only inside the kernel)
    u1[i]: in DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    u2[i]: in DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    v1[j]: in DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    v2[j]: in DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    y[j]:  in DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    z[i]:  in DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i

    # Input/output vectors (updated in the kernel)
    x[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    w[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i

    # Temporaries introduced for optimization
    # y_beta holds β * y, to avoid multiplying by β inside the N×N loop
    y_beta[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    # x_alpha holds α * x after x has been updated, 
    # so α is not multiplied inside the N×N loop for w
    x_alpha[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j

parameters:
    N: index_type                 # matrix / vector size
    alpha: DATA_TYPE              # scalar α
    beta:  DATA_TYPE              # scalar β

    # Tunable blocking and vectorization parameters
    TI: index_type                # tile size for i (e.g., 64)
    TJ: index_type                # tile size for j (e.g., 64)
    TJ_x: index_type              # tile size for j in x-update (e.g., 256)
    VEC: index_type               # SIMD width in elements (e.g., 4 for double on AVX2)

computation:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Rank-1 updates:
    #    A := A + u1 * v1^T + u2 * v2^T
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    A_update:
        for i, j:
            A[i, j] = A[i, j] + u1[i] * v1[j] + u2[i] * v2[j]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Pre-scale y by β to reduce multiplications in the A^T * y phase:
    #    y_beta[j] = β * y[j]
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    scale_y:
        for j:
            y_beta[j] = beta * y[j]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Compute:
    #       x[i] := x[i] + β * (A^T y)[i] + z[i]
    #    using the pre-scaled y_beta:
    #       x[i] := x[i] + sum_j A[j, i] * y_beta[j] + z[i]
    #
    #    This fuses the original second and third loops while preserving
    #    the mathematical result for x.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    x_update:
        for i:
            x[i] = x[i] + sum(j, A[j, i] * y_beta[j]) + z[i]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Pre-scale x by α once, instead of multiplying by α inside the
    #    N×N loop for w:
    #       x_alpha[j] = α * x[j]
    #    This preserves the final x and w semantics:
    #       original: w := w + α * A * x
    #       now:      w := w + A * (α * x) = w + α * A * x
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    scale_x:
        for j:
            x_alpha[j] = alpha * x[j]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Final matrix-vector product:
    #       w[i] := w[i] + α * (A x)[i]
    #    implemented as:
    #       w[i] := w[i] + sum_j A[i, j] * x_alpha[j]
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    w_update:
        for i:
            w[i] = w[i] + sum(j, A[i, j] * x_alpha[j])

dependencies:
    # A must be fully updated before it is used in x_update and w_update
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):
        A_update(i, j) -> x_update(i)   # x_update(i) uses A[j, i] for all j
        A_update(i, j) -> w_update(i)   # w_update(i) uses A[i, j] for all j

    # scale_y must finish before x_update uses y_beta
    for i in [0, N):
        scale_y(*) -> x_update(i)

    # scale_x must finish before w_update uses x_alpha
    for i in [0, N):
        scale_x(*) -> w_update(i)

optimization:
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # General goals:
    #   - Improve cache locality via 2D blocking (tiling) on A.
    #   - Reduce scalar multiplications by hoisting α and β out of
    #     the N×N loops (done structurally via y_beta and x_alpha).
    #   - Exploit outer-loop parallelism across i-tiles and i-rows.
    #   - Vectorize inner loops over j where A is accessed contiguously.
    # --------------------------------------------------------------

    # 1) 2D blocking for loops that traverse A row-wise (A_update, w_update).
    #    This increases temporal locality in A and in the vectors v1, v2, x_alpha.
    block(i, Ii, TI)      # i = Ii * TI + ii
    block(j, Jj, TJ)      # j = Jj * TJ + jj
    hoist(Ii)             # move tile loops Ii, Jj outermost
    hoist(Jj)

    # 2) Additional 1D blocking for the j dimension in x_update's reduction.
    #    This improves reuse of y_beta[j] and keeps partial A columns in cache.
    block(j, Jx, TJ_x)

    # 3) Parallelism:
    #    - A_update: different rows (and tiles of rows) of A are independent.
    #    - scale_y, scale_x: each element is independent.
    #    - x_update: each x[i] is an independent reduction over j.
    #    - w_update: each w[i] is an independent reduction over j.
    #
    #    We therefore parallelize the outer i-like dimensions.
    parallelize(Ii)       # tile-parallelism for A_update and w_update
    parallelize(i)        # row-parallelism for x_update
    parallelize(j)        # element-parallelism for scale_y and scale_x

    # 4) Vectorization:
    #    - A[i, j] is contiguous in j (row-major), so vectorize j where
    #      A is accessed as A[i, j].
    #    - In x_update, the reduction is over j, so we also vectorize j.
    vectorize(j, VEC)     # encourage SIMD on inner j loops

    # 5) Unrolling:
    #    Unroll inner j loops moderately to reduce loop-control overhead
    #    and expose more ILP for the compiler and hardware.
    unroll(j, 4)

    # 6) Scalar hoisting:
    #    Although reflected structurally in the computation, conceptually:
    #      - Treat beta as hoisted into y_beta (one multiply per j).
    #      - Treat alpha as hoisted into x_alpha (one multiply per j).
    #    This removes multiplications by α and β from the O(N^2) loops.
    #    (No explicit directive needed beyond the temp arrays.)
--- END OF MODEL: gemver-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: gemver-03 ---
domain:
    # Single problem size N; all loops iterate over [0, N)
    i: dim in [0, N)          # generic row index
    j: dim in [0, N)          # generic column index

data:
    # Row-major N×N matrix A
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # row-major

    # Input vectors
    u1[i]: in  DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    u2[i]: in  DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    v1[j]: in  DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    v2[j]: in  DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    y[i]:  in  DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    z[i]:  in  DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i

    # Output / temporary vectors
    x[i]:  temp DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i   # x is fully overwritten in the kernel
    w[i]:  out  DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i

    # Optional helper to reduce arithmetic in x computation:
    beta_y[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j   # stores beta * y[j]

parameters:
    N: int
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable blocking / SIMD parameters (chosen for target x64 machine).
    TI: int    # tile size in i-dimension (rows), e.g., 64
    TJ: int    # tile size in j-dimension (cols), e.g., 64
    VEC: int   # SIMD vector width along contiguous dimension (e.g., 8 for AVX2 doubles)

computation:
    # 1) Rank‑1 update: A := A + u1 v1ᵀ + u2 v2ᵀ
    UPDATE_A:
        for i, j:
            A[i, j] = A[i, j] + u1[i] * v1[j] + u2[i] * v2[j]

    # 2) x := beta * Aᵀ y + z
    #    The original code does:
    #      x[i] += beta * A[j][i] * y[j]   (double loop)
    #      x[i] += z[i]                    (single loop)
    #    with x initialized to 0.
    #    Mathematically: x[i] = z[i] + beta * sum_j A[j, i] * y[j].
    PRECOMPUTE_BETA_Y:
        for j:
            beta_y[j] = beta * y[j]

    COMPUTE_X:
        for i:
            x[i] = z[i] + sum(j, A[j, i] * beta_y[j])

    # 3) w := alpha * A x
    #    Original: w[i] += alpha * A[i][j] * x[j] with w initialized to 0,
    #    so w[i] = alpha * sum_j A[i, j] * x[j].
    COMPUTE_W:
        for i:
            w[i] = alpha * sum(j, A[i, j] * x[j])

dependencies:
    # A must be fully updated before it is used in x or w.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, N), i2 in [0, N):
        UPDATE_A(i, j) -> COMPUTE_X(i2)
        UPDATE_A(i, j) -> COMPUTE_W(i2)

    # x must be fully computed before it is used in w.
    for i in [0, N), i2 in [0, N):
        COMPUTE_X(i) -> COMPUTE_W(i2)

optimization:
    #-----------------------------------------
    # 1) Optimize UPDATE_A: A += u1 v1ᵀ + u2 v2ᵀ
    #-----------------------------------------
    UPDATE_A:
        # Block over rows and columns so that working tiles of A, v1, v2
        # stay in L1/L2 cache.
        block(i, I_A, TI)      # outer tile index I_A, tile size TI in i
        block(j, J_A, TJ)      # outer tile index J_A, tile size TJ in j

        # Parallelize across row tiles: each thread updates disjoint rows of A.
        parallelize(I_A)

        # Within a row, j is contiguous in memory (row-major), good for SIMD.
        vectorize(j, VEC)

        # Hoist per-row invariants out of the inner j-loop:
        #   t1 = u1[i]; t2 = u2[i];
        #   A[i, j] += t1 * v1[j] + t2 * v2[j];
        hoist(i)

    #-----------------------------------------
    # 2) Optimize COMPUTE_X: x = z + beta * Aᵀ y
    #-----------------------------------------
    PRECOMPUTE_BETA_Y:
        # Simple vector multiply; trivially vectorizable and parallelizable.
        parallelize(j)
        vectorize(j, VEC)

    COMPUTE_X:
        # Implement as a cache-friendly sweep over rows of A:
        #   for j in [0,N):
        #       t = beta_y[j]
        #       for i in [0,N):
        #           x[i] += A[j, i] * t
        # This is equivalent to the reduction formulation above and
        # converts the column access A[*, i] into contiguous row access A[j, *].
        interchange(i, j)   # j outer, i inner for this kernel

        # Vectorize inner loop over i; A[j, i] is contiguous in i after interchange.
        vectorize(i, VEC)

        # Optional parallelization over j requires treating x as a reduction:
        # each thread accumulates into a private x_local[i] and these are
        # summed at the end. This adds O(#threads * N) extra storage, which
        # remains well below the 50% memory overhead bound since A is O(N²).
        parallelize(j)

    #-----------------------------------------
    # 3) Optimize COMPUTE_W: w = alpha * A x
    #-----------------------------------------
    COMPUTE_W:
        # Use the natural row-major traversal: i outer, j inner.
        block(i, I_W, TI)      # reuse the same row blocking as in UPDATE_A
        parallelize(I_W)       # distribute row tiles across threads

        # j is contiguous in memory along each row of A.
        vectorize(j, VEC)

        # Hoist per-row invariant alpha and reuse x[j] loaded once per chunk.
        hoist(i)

    #-----------------------------------------
    # General notes:
    # - All reductions over j are expressed via sum(j, ...), enabling
    #   the compiler/runtime to implement them with thread-local
    #   accumulators plus a final combine step if parallelized.
    # - Extra memory:
    #     * beta_y[N] (one additional N-vector),
    #     * optional per-thread reduction buffers of size O(N),
    #   which keeps the total memory footprint within 50% of the original
    #   (dominated by the N×N matrix A).
--- END OF MODEL: gemver-03 ---

domain:
    i: dim in [0, n)
    j: dim in [0, n)

data:
    # Matrix A is stored column-major to make all three uses of A contiguous
    # in the innermost loop after suitable loop interchanges.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> j * n + i  # column-major n x n

    # Input vectors (read-only in the kernel)
    u1[i]: in DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    v1[j]: in DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    u2[i]: in DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    v2[j]: in DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    y[i]:  in DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    z[i]:  in DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i

    # Output / updated vectors
    x[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    w[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i

    # Temporary, kernel-local vectors used only to reduce arithmetic and
    # improve locality; their size is O(n), well within the 50% memory budget.
    y_beta[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j       # y scaled by beta
    x_alpha[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j      # final x scaled by alpha

parameters:
    n: int                   # problem size (N in the C code)
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable optimization parameters (chosen empirically for the target x64)
    T: int                   # tile size for i and j (e.g., 64)
    V: int                   # SIMD vector width (e.g., 8 for AVX2 doubles)
    P: int                   # max parallel worker count (<= available cores)

computation:
    # 0. Pre-scale y by beta once, to avoid recomputing beta * y[j] inside the
    #    O(n^2) x-update loop.
    scale_y_beta:
        for j:
            y_beta[j] = beta * y[j]

    # 1. Rank-2 update: A := A + u1 v1^T + u2 v2^T
    #    Semantically:
    #      ∀i,j: A[i,j] = A[i,j] + u1[i]*v1[j] + u2[i]*v2[j]
    update_A:
        for i, j:
            A[i, j] = A[i, j] + u1[i] * v1[j] + u2[i] * v2[j]

    # 2. x := x + beta * A^T * y
    #    Using y_beta, this becomes:
    #      ∀i: x[i] = x[i] + sum_j A[j,i] * y_beta[j]
    update_x:
        for i:
            x[i] = x[i] + sum(j, A[j, i] * y_beta[j])

    # 3. x := x + z
    add_z:
        for i:
            x[i] = x[i] + z[i]

    # 4. Pre-scale final x by alpha, to avoid recomputing alpha * x[j] inside
    #    the O(n^2) w-update loop.
    scale_x_alpha:
        for j:
            x_alpha[j] = alpha * x[j]

    # 5. w := w + alpha * A * x  =  w + A * x_alpha
    #    Semantically:
    #      ∀i: w[i] = w[i] + sum_j A[i,j] * x_alpha[j]
    update_w:
        for i:
            w[i] = w[i] + sum(j, A[i, j] * x_alpha[j])

dependencies:
    # A must be fully updated before it is used in either matrix-vector product.
    for i in [0, n), j in [0, n):
        update_A(i, j) -> update_x(i)
        update_A(i, j) -> update_w(i)

    # All y_beta elements are needed before any x[i] is updated.
    for j in [0, n), i in [0, n):
        scale_y_beta(j) -> update_x(i)

    # For each component k, x[k] is updated by update_x before add_z,
    # and then add_z(k) must finish before scale_x_alpha(k).
    for k in [0, n):
        update_x(k) -> add_z(k)
        add_z(k) -> scale_x_alpha(k)

    # x_alpha must be fully computed before any element of w is updated.
    for j in [0, n), i in [0, n):
        scale_x_alpha(j) -> update_w(i)

optimization:
    #----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # High-level strategy
    #  - Store A in column-major form so that accesses A[*,j] are contiguous.
    #    With appropriate loop orders, all three uses of A (rank-2 update,
    #    A^T*y, and A*x) get good spatial locality.
    #  - Use two O(n) temporaries (y_beta, x_alpha) to cut the number of
    #    multiplies in the two gemv-like phases roughly in half:
    #       original:  ~4 n^2 multiplies
    #       optimized: ~2 n^2 + O(n) multiplies
    #  - Tile i and j to keep working sets of A in cache.
    #  - Parallelize over outer tiles / rows where there are no dependencies.
    #  - Vectorize the innermost loops.
    #----------------------------------------------------------------------

    #--- Rank-2 update: A = A + u1 v1^T + u2 v2^T ------------------------
    update_A:
        # With column-major A, we want j fixed while i varies fastest so that
        # A[i,j] is accessed contiguously in memory. Thus iterate columns j in
        # the outer loop and rows i inside.
        interchange(i, j)          # loop order: for j in ..., for i in ...

        # Tile A to improve cache reuse of u1/u2 rows and v1/v2 columns.
        block(j, J_A, T)           # tile columns of A
        block(i, I_A, T)           # tile rows of A inside each column tile
        hoist(J_A)                 # outermost: iterate column tiles
        hoist(I_A)                 # next: iterate row tiles inside each column tile

        # Each (J_A) tile owns a disjoint set of columns of A, so it is safe
        # to parallelize across J_A without synchronization.
        parallelize(J_A)           # distribute column tiles across up to P threads

        # Within a tile, rows i are contiguous in memory for fixed j, so
        # vectorize across i.
        vectorize(i, V)
        unroll(i, 4)               # small unroll to reduce loop overhead

    #--- x := x + A^T * (beta*y) ----------------------------------------
    scale_y_beta:
        # Simple 1D loop over y: memory-bound, so expose both thread and SIMD
        # parallelism.
        parallelize(j)
        vectorize(j, V)

    update_x:
        # With column-major A, A[j,i] is contiguous as j varies (A[j,i] index
        # is i*n + j). The original loop order (i outer, j inner) already
        # yields unit-stride access in j for each x[i], so we keep that order.
        #
        # Each x[i] is an independent reduction over j, so we parallelize
        # across blocks of i.
        block(i, I_x, T)
        hoist(I_x)
        parallelize(I_x)           # independent reductions for different x[i]

        block(j, J_x, T)           # optional j-tiling to keep y_beta and A tiles in cache
        vectorize(j, V)            # vectorize along contiguous j
        unroll(j, 4)

    #--- x := x + z ------------------------------------------------------
    add_z:
        # Purely element-wise; no cross-iteration dependencies.
        parallelize(i)
        vectorize(i, V)
        unroll(i, 4)

    #--- x_alpha[j] = alpha * x[j] --------------------------------------
    scale_x_alpha:
        # Another simple 1D loop; parallelize and vectorize over j.
        parallelize(j)
        vectorize(j, V)

    #--- w := w + A * x_alpha -------------------------------------------
    update_w:
        # We want:
        #   - each w[i] to be updated only by a single thread (no reductions),
        #   - A[i,j] accesses to be contiguous in the innermost loop.
        #
        # To achieve this with column-major A, we:
        #   - block the row dimension i and distribute row-tiles (I_w) across
        #     threads, so each thread owns a disjoint subset of w[i],
        #   - within each (I_w, J_w) tile, iterate j outside i so that A[i,j]
        #     is accessed as a contiguous column segment.
        block(i, I_w, T)           # tile rows; these tiles will be thread-owned
        block(j, J_w, T)           # tile columns for cache
        hoist(I_w)                 # outermost: tiles of rows
        hoist(J_w)                 # next: tiles of columns
        parallelize(I_w)           # distribute row tiles across up to P threads

        # Within each (I_w, J_w) tile, swap i and j so j varies faster:
        #   for j in J_w:
        #     for i in I_w:
        #       w[i] += A[i,j] * x_alpha[j];
        # For fixed j, A[i,j] is contiguous as i varies in column-major layout.
        interchange(i, j)

        vectorize(i, V)            # vectorize across contiguous i
        unroll(i, 4)

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # Matrices/vectors; all are logically dense.
    # A is stored row-major: A[i, j] at address base_A + (i * N + j)
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    u1[i]: in    DATA_TYPE = i -> i              # 1D, stride-1
    v1[j]: in    DATA_TYPE = j -> j              # 1D, stride-1
    u2[i]: in    DATA_TYPE = i -> i
    v2[j]: in    DATA_TYPE = j -> j
    w[i]:  inout DATA_TYPE = i -> i
    x[i]:  inout DATA_TYPE = i -> i
    y[i]:  in    DATA_TYPE = i -> i
    z[i]:  in    DATA_TYPE = i -> i

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tuning parameters for the kernel (chosen based on cache/SIMD width).
    Ti: int  # tile size along i (rows),  e.g., 64 or 128
    Tj: int  # tile size along j (cols),  e.g., 64 or 128
    V:  int  # SIMD width, e.g., 4 or 8 doubles / 8 or 16 floats
    U:  int  # unroll factor for the innermost loop, e.g., 4

computation:
    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Rank-2 update:
    #    A := A + u1 v1^T + u2 v2^T
    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    A_update:
        for i, j:
            A[i, j] = A[i, j] + u1[i] * v1[j] + u2[i] * v2[j]

    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    # 2+3. x := x + beta * A^T y + z
    #
    # Original code:
    #   for (i) for (j) x[i] += beta * A[j][i] * y[j];
    #   for (i)          x[i] += z[i];
    #
    # Mathematical form (used here):
    #   x[i] = x[i] + beta * sum_j (A[j, i] * y[j]) + z[i]
    #
    # Note: A on RHS is the updated matrix produced by A_update.
    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    X_update:
        for i:
            x[i] = x[i] + beta * sum(j, A[j, i] * y[j]) + z[i]

    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Final GEMV:
    #    w := w + alpha * A x
    #
    # Original code:
    #   for (i) for (j) w[i] += alpha * A[i][j] * x[j];
    #
    # Mathematical form:
    #   w[i] = w[i] + alpha * sum_j (A[i, j] * x[j])
    #
    # Again A is the updated matrix from A_update, and x is the
    # fully updated vector (after X_update).
    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    W_update:
        for i:
            w[i] = w[i] + alpha * sum(j, A[i, j] * x[j])

dependencies:
    # A must be updated everywhere before its uses in X_update and W_update.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):
        A_update(i, j) -> X_update(i)
        A_update(i, j) -> W_update(i)

    # x must be fully updated (including the "+ z" term) before W_update.
    for i in [0, N):
        X_update(i) -> W_update(i)

optimization:
    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    # Conventions:
    #   - block(d, Dtile, T): split dimension d into an outer tile
    #     index Dtile and an inner point index d with tile size T.
    #   - hoist(Dtile): move Dtile to the outermost position in the
    #     loop nest where it is used.
    #   - parallelize(d): execute iterations along dimension d in
    #     parallel (e.g., OpenMP parallel for).
    #   - vectorize(d, V): implement dimension d with SIMD of width V.
    #   - unroll(d, U): unroll loops over dimension d by factor U.
    #   - fuse(L1, L2, d): execute statements L1 and L2 in a single
    #     loop nest along dimension d when dependences allow it.
    #
    # All transformations must preserve the data dependences declared
    # above; in particular, A_update happens before X_update and
    # W_update, and X_update before W_update.
    #-----------------------------------------------------------

    #===========================================================
    # 1. Optimize rank-2 update: A_update
    #===========================================================
    A_update:
        # Tile A in 2D for cache locality.
        block(i, Ii, Ti)          # Ii: tile index for rows
        block(j, Jj, Tj)          # Jj: tile index for columns

        hoist(Ii)                 # Outer: Ii
        hoist(Jj)                 # Then: Jj

        # Parallelize across row tiles: rows are independent.
        parallelize(Ii)

        # Within each tile, traverse rows then columns so that
        # A[i, j], v1[j], v2[j] are accessed contiguously in j.
        # The innermost j-loop is vectorized and unrolled.
        vectorize(j, V)
        unroll(j, U)

        # The compiler is expected to introduce per-row temporaries:
        #   u1_i = u1[i]; u2_i = u2[i];
        # so that multiplications with v1[j]/v2[j] reuse u1_i/u2_i.

    #===========================================================
    # 2. Optimize x := x + beta * A^T y + z
    #===========================================================
    X_update:
        # Treat the "beta * A^T y" part as a reduction over j.
        # We implement this reduction using a row-wise sweep of A
        # to exploit A's row-major layout.
        #
        # Equivalent row-wise algorithm:
        #   // x starts with its input value
        #   for j in [0, N):                     // sweep rows of A
        #       t = beta * y[j]
        #       for i in [0, N):                 // sweep columns
        #           x[i] += t * A[j, i]          // use A row j
        #   for i in [0, N):
        #       x[i] += z[i]
        #
        # This still realizes:
        #   x[i] = x_in[i] + beta * sum_j A[j, i]*y[j] + z[i].

        # Implement the reduction with j as the outer loop and
        # i as the inner loop to get row-major access A[j, i].
        # (The "sum(j, ...)" is lowered that way.)
        hoist(j)                  # j outermost in the reduction nest

        # Fuse the reduction with A_update along the shared row
        # dimension j so that each row A[j, *] is:
        #   - updated (rank-2 update),
        #   - immediately used in the A^T y multiplication.
        #
        # Fused per-row kernel (conceptual):
        #   for j in [0, N):
        #       u1_j = u1[j]
        #       u2_j = u2[j]
        #       t    = beta * y[j]
        #       for i in [0, N):
        #           # rank-2 update
        #           A[j, i] += u1_j * v1[i] + u2_j * v2[i]
        #           # contribution to x from row j of A
        #           x[i]    += t * A[j, i]
        #
        # This obeys all dependences because X_update is a
        # pure reduction over j and we use the updated A[j,i].
        fuse(A_update, X_update, j)

        # Parallelize and vectorize along i inside each row j:
        #   - A[j, i], v1[i], v2[i], x[i] are contiguous,
        #   - each (j, i) pair updates a distinct x[i] in the
        #     inner loop, so parallelization over i is safe.
        parallelize(i)
        vectorize(i, V)
        unroll(i, U)

        # After finishing the fused reduction over j (i.e., after
        # beta * A^T y has been accumulated into x), perform
        # x[i] += z[i] as a separate, simple, fully parallel loop:
        #
        #   for i in [0, N):
        #       x[i] += z[i]
        #
        # (This loop is conceptually part of X_update and must
        #  run after the reduction has completed.)
        parallelize(i)
        vectorize(i, V)
        unroll(i, U)

    #===========================================================
    # 3. Optimize final GEMV: w := w + alpha * A x
    #===========================================================
    W_update:
        # Tile A over (i, j) to exploit cache reuse of x[j] across
        # multiple rows and improve TLB behavior.
        block(i, Ii_w, Ti)
        block(j, Jj_w, Tj)

        hoist(Ii_w)               # Outer: tiles of rows
        hoist(Jj_w)               # Then: tiles of columns

        # Distribute row tiles across threads; each thread accumulates
        # into distinct segments of w.
        parallelize(Ii_w)

        # Within each row i:
        #   - iterate j as the innermost loop,
        #   - access A[i, j] and x[j] contiguously in j,
        #   - use a scalar accumulator 's' for w[i]:
        #       s = w[i];
        #       for j: s += alpha * A[i, j] * x[j];
        #       w[i] = s;
        #
        # The innermost j-loop is vectorized and unrolled.
        vectorize(j, V)
        unroll(j, U)

/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE *alpha,
		 DATA_TYPE *beta,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(u1,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(v1,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(u2,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(v2,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(w,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(z,N,n))
{
  int i, j;

  *alpha = 1.5;
  *beta = 1.2;

  DATA_TYPE fn = (DATA_TYPE)n;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      u1[i] = i;
      u2[i] = ((i+1)/fn)/2.0;
      v1[i] = ((i+1)/fn)/4.0;
      v2[i] = ((i+1)/fn)/6.0;
      y[i] = ((i+1)/fn)/8.0;
      z[i] = ((i+1)/fn)/9.0;
      x[i] = 0.0;
      w[i] = 0.0;
      for (j = 0; j < n; j++)
        A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*j % n) / n;
    }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(w,N,n))
{
  int i;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("w");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, w[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("w");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_gemver[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
		   DATA_TYPE alpha,
		   DATA_TYPE beta,
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(u1,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(v1,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(u2,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(v2,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(w,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(z,N,n))
{
  int i, j;

#pragma scop

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++)
      A[i][j] = A[i][j] + u1[i] * v1[j] + u2[i] * v2[j];

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++)
      x[i] = x[i] + beta * A[j][i] * y[j];

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    x[i] = x[i] + z[i];

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++)
      w[i] = w[i] +  alpha * A[i][j] * x[j];

#pragma endscop
}

{

  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(v2, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(w, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(x, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(y, DATA_TYPE, N, n);

    #    With appropriate loop orders, all three uses of A (rank-2 update,
    #    A^T*y, and A*x) get good spatial locality.
    #  - Use two O(n) temporaries (y_beta, x_alpha) to cut the number of
    #    multiplies in the two gemv-like phases roughly in half:
    #       original:  ~4 n^2 multiplies
    #       optimized: ~2 n^2 + O(n) multiplies
    #  - Tile i and j to keep working sets of A in cache.
    #  - Parallelize over outer tiles / rows where there are no dependencies.
    #  - Vectorize the innermost loops.
    #----------------------------------------------------------------------

    #--- Rank-2 update: A = A + u1 v1^T + u2 v2^T ------------------------
    update_A:
        # With column-major A, we want j fixed while i varies fastest so that
        # A[i,j] is accessed contiguously in memory. Thus iterate columns j in
        # the outer loop and rows i inside.
        interchange(i, j)          # loop order: for j in ..., for i in ...

        # Tile A to improve cache reuse of u1/u2 rows and v1/v2 columns.
        block(j, J_A, T)           # tile columns of A
        block(i, I_A, T)           # tile rows of A inside each column tile
        hoist(J_A)                 # outermost: iterate column tiles
        hoist(I_A)                 # next: iterate row tiles inside each column tile

        # Each (J_A) tile owns a disjoint set of columns of A, so it is safe
        # to parallelize across J_A without synchronization.
        parallelize(J_A)           # distribute column tiles across up to P threads

        # Within a tile, rows i are contiguous in memory for fixed j, so
        # vectorize across i.
        vectorize(i, V)
        unroll(i, 4)               # small unroll to reduce loop overhead

    #--- x := x + A^T * (beta*y) ----------------------------------------
    scale_y_beta:
        # Simple 1D loop over y: memory-bound, so expose both thread and SIMD
        # parallelism.
        parallelize(j)
        vectorize(j, V)

    update_x:
        # With column-major A, A[j,i] is contiguous as j varies (A[j,i] index
        # is i*n + j). The original loop order (i outer, j inner) already
        # yields unit-stride access in j for each x[i], so we keep that order.
        #
        # Each x[i] is an independent reduction over j, so we parallelize
        # across blocks of i.
        block(i, I_x, T)
        hoist(I_x)
        parallelize(I_x)           # independent reductions for different x[i]

        block(j, J_x, T)           # optional j-tiling to keep y_beta and A tiles in cache
        vectorize(j, V)            # vectorize along contiguous j
        unroll(j, 4)

    #--- x := x + z ------------------------------------------------------
    add_z:
        # Purely element-wise; no cross-iteration dependencies.
        parallelize(i)
        vectorize(i, V)
        unroll(i, 4)

    #--- x_alpha[j] = alpha * x[j] --------------------------------------
    scale_x_alpha:
        # Another simple 1D loop; parallelize and vectorize over j.
        parallelize(j)
        vectorize(j, V)

    #--- w := w + A * x_alpha -------------------------------------------
    update_w:
        # We want:
        #   - each w[i] to be updated only by a single thread (no reductions),
        #   - A[i,j] accesses to be contiguous in the innermost loop.
        #
        # To achieve this with column-major A, we:
        #   - block the row dimension i and distribute row-tiles (I_w) across
        #     threads, so each thread owns a disjoint subset of w[i],
        #   - within each (I_w, J_w) tile, iterate j outside i so that A[i,j]
        #     is accessed as a contiguous column segment.
        block(i, I_w, T)           # tile rows; these tiles will be thread-owned
        block(j, J_w, T)           # tile columns for cache
        hoist(I_w)                 # outermost: tiles of rows
        hoist(J_w)                 # next: tiles of columns
        parallelize(I_w)           # distribute row tiles across up to P threads

        # Within each (I_w, J_w) tile, swap i and j so j varies faster:
        #   for j in J_w:
        #     for i in I_w:
        #       w[i] += A[i,j] * x_alpha[j];
        # For fixed j, A[i,j] is contiguous as i varies in column-major layout.
        interchange(i, j)

        vectorize(i, V)            # vectorize across contiguous i
        unroll(i, 4)

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # Matrices/vectors; all are logically dense.
    # A is stored row-major: A[i, j] at address base_A + (i * N + j)
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    u1[i]: in    DATA_TYPE = i -> i              # 1D, stride-1
    v1[j]: in    DATA_TYPE = j -> j              # 1D, stride-1
    u2[i]: in    DATA_TYPE = i -> i
    v2[j]: in    DATA_TYPE = j -> j
    w[i]:  inout DATA_TYPE = i -> i
    x[i]:  inout DATA_TYPE = i -> i
    y[i]:  in    DATA_TYPE = i -> i
    z[i]:  in    DATA_TYPE = i -> i

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tuning parameters for the kernel (chosen based on cache/SIMD width).
    Ti: int  # tile size along i (rows),  e.g., 64 or 128
    Tj: int  # tile size along j (cols),  e.g., 64 or 128
    V:  int  # SIMD width, e.g., 4 or 8 doubles / 8 or 16 floats
    U:  int  # unroll factor for the innermost loop, e.g., 4

computation:
    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Rank-2 update:
    #    A := A + u1 v1^T + u2 v2^T
    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    A_update:
        for i, j:
            A[i, j] = A[i, j] + u1[i] * v1[j] + u2[i] * v2[j]

    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    # 2+3. x := x + beta * A^T y + z
    #
    # Original code:
    #   for (i) for (j) x[i] += beta * A[j][i] * y[j];
    #   for (i)          x[i] += z[i];
    #
    # Mathematical form (used here):
    #   x[i] = x[i] + beta * sum_j (A[j, i] * y[j]) + z[i]
    #
    # Note: A on RHS is the updated matrix produced by A_update.
    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    X_update:
        for i:
            x[i] = x[i] + beta * sum(j, A[j, i] * y[j]) + z[i]

    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Final GEMV:
    #    w := w + alpha * A x
    #
    # Original code:
    #   for (i) for (j) w[i] += alpha * A[i][j] * x[j];
    #
    # Mathematical form:
    #   w[i] = w[i] + alpha * sum_j (A[i, j] * x[j])
    #
    # Again A is the updated matrix from A_update, and x is the
    # fully updated vector (after X_update).
    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    W_update:
        for i:
            w[i] = w[i] + alpha * sum(j, A[i, j] * x[j])

dependencies:
    # A must be updated everywhere before its uses in X_update and W_update.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):
        A_update(i, j) -> X_update(i)
        A_update(i, j) -> W_update(i)

    # x must be fully updated (including the "+ z" term) before W_update.
    for i in [0, N):
        X_update(i) -> W_update(i)

optimization:
    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    # Conventions:
    #   - block(d, Dtile, T): split dimension d into an outer tile
    #     index Dtile and an inner point index d with tile size T.
    #   - hoist(Dtile): move Dtile to the outermost position in the
    #     loop nest where it is used.
    #   - parallelize(d): execute iterations along dimension d in
    #     parallel (e.g., OpenMP parallel for).
    #   - vectorize(d, V): implement dimension d with SIMD of width V.
    #   - unroll(d, U): unroll loops over dimension d by factor U.
    #   - fuse(L1, L2, d): execute statements L1 and L2 in a single
    #     loop nest along dimension d when dependences allow it.
    #
    # All transformations must preserve the data dependences declared
    # above; in particular, A_update happens before X_update and
    # W_update, and X_update before W_update.
    #-----------------------------------------------------------

    #===========================================================
    # 1. Optimize rank-2 update: A_update
    #===========================================================
    A_update:
        # Tile A in 2D for cache locality.
        block(i, Ii, Ti)          # Ii: tile index for rows
        block(j, Jj, Tj)          # Jj: tile index for columns

        hoist(Ii)                 # Outer: Ii
        hoist(Jj)                 # Then: Jj

        # Parallelize across row tiles: rows are independent.
        parallelize(Ii)

        # Within each tile, traverse rows then columns so that
        # A[i, j], v1[j], v2[j] are accessed contiguously in j.
        # The innermost j-loop is vectorized and unrolled.
        vectorize(j, V)
        unroll(j, U)

        # The compiler is expected to introduce per-row temporaries:
        #   u1_i = u1[i]; u2_i = u2[i];
        # so that multiplications with v1[j]/v2[j] reuse u1_i/u2_i.

    #===========================================================
    # 2. Optimize x := x + beta * A^T y + z
    #===========================================================
    X_update:
        # Treat the "beta * A^T y" part as a reduction over j.
        # We implement this reduction using a row-wise sweep of A
        # to exploit A's row-major layout.
        #
        # Equivalent row-wise algorithm:
        #   // x starts with its input value
        #   for j in [0, N):                     // sweep rows of A
        #       t = beta * y[j]
        #       for i in [0, N):                 // sweep columns
        #           x[i] += t * A[j, i]          // use A row j
        #   for i in [0, N):
        #       x[i] += z[i]
        #
        # This still realizes:
        #   x[i] = x_in[i] + beta * sum_j A[j, i]*y[j] + z[i].

        # Implement the reduction with j as the outer loop and
        # i as the inner loop to get row-major access A[j, i].
        # (The "sum(j, ...)" is lowered that way.)
        hoist(j)                  # j outermost in the reduction nest

        # Fuse the reduction with A_update along the shared row
        # dimension j so that each row A[j, *] is:
        #   - updated (rank-2 update),
        #   - immediately used in the A^T y multiplication.
        #
        # Fused per-row kernel (conceptual):
        #   for j in [0, N):
        #       u1_j = u1[j]
        #       u2_j = u2[j]
        #       t    = beta * y[j]
        #       for i in [0, N):
        #           # rank-2 update
        #           A[j, i] += u1_j * v1[i] + u2_j * v2[i]
        #           # contribution to x from row j of A
        #           x[i]    += t * A[j, i]
        #
        # This obeys all dependences because X_update is a
        # pure reduction over j and we use the updated A[j,i].
        fuse(A_update, X_update, j)

        # Parallelize and vectorize along i inside each row j:
        #   - A[j, i], v1[i], v2[i], x[i] are contiguous,
        #   - each (j, i) pair updates a distinct x[i] in the
        #     inner loop, so parallelization over i is safe.
        parallelize(i)
        vectorize(i, V)
        unroll(i, U)

        # After finishing the fused reduction over j (i.e., after
        # beta * A^T y has been accumulated into x), perform
        # x[i] += z[i] as a separate, simple, fully parallel loop:
        #
        #   for i in [0, N):
        #       x[i] += z[i]
        #
        # (This loop is conceptually part of X_update and must
        #  run after the reduction has completed.)
        parallelize(i)
        vectorize(i, V)
        unroll(i, U)

    #===========================================================
    # 3. Optimize final GEMV: w := w + alpha * A x
    #===========================================================
    W_update:
        # Tile A over (i, j) to exploit cache reuse of x[j] across
        # multiple rows and improve TLB behavior.
        block(i, Ii_w, Ti)
        block(j, Jj_w, Tj)

        hoist(Ii_w)               # Outer: tiles of rows
        hoist(Jj_w)               # Then: tiles of columns

        # Distribute row tiles across threads; each thread accumulates
        # into distinct segments of w.
        parallelize(Ii_w)

        # Within each row i:
        #   - iterate j as the innermost loop,
        #   - access A[i, j] and x[j] contiguously in j,
        #   - use a scalar accumulator 's' for w[i]:
        #       s = w[i];
        #       for j: s += alpha * A[i, j] * x[j];
        #       w[i] = s;
        #
        # The innermost j-loop is vectorized and unrolled.
        vectorize(j, V)
        unroll(j, U)

#include <stdio.h>

#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "gemver.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE *alpha,
		 DATA_TYPE *beta,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(u1,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(v1,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(u2,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(v2,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(w,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(z,N,n))
{
  int i, j;

  *alpha = 1.5;
  *beta = 1.2;

  DATA_TYPE fn = (DATA_TYPE)n;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      u1[i] = i;
      u2[i] = ((i+1)/fn)/2.0;
      v1[i] = ((i+1)/fn)/4.0;
      v2[i] = ((i+1)/fn)/6.0;
      y[i] = ((i+1)/fn)/8.0;
      z[i] = ((i+1)/fn)/9.0;
      x[i] = 0.0;
      w[i] = 0.0;
      for (j = 0; j < n; j++)
        A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*j % n) / n;
    }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(w,N,n))
{
  int i;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("w");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, w[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("w");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_gemver[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
		   DATA_TYPE alpha,
		   DATA_TYPE beta,
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(u1,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(v1,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(u2,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(v2,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(w,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(z,N,n))
{
  int i, j;

#pragma scop

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++)
      A[i][j] = A[i][j] + u1[i] * v1[j] + u2[i] * v2[j];

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++)
      x[i] = x[i] + beta * A[j][i] * y[j];

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    x[i] = x[i] + z[i];

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_N; j++)
      w[i] = w[i] +  alpha * A[i][j] * x[j];

#pragma endscop
}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  DATA_TYPE alpha;
  DATA_TYPE beta;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(u1, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(v1, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(u2, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(v2, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(w, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(x, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(y, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(z, DATA_TYPE, N, n);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, &alpha, &beta,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u1),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(v1),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u2),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(v2),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(w),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(z));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_gemver (n, alpha, beta,
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u1),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(v1),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(u2),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(v2),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(w),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(z));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(w)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(u1);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(v1);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(u2);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(v2);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(w);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(x);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(y);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(z);

  return 0;
}

# Optimized polyhedral-style model for gemver

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # Dense matrix A, row-major
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Input / inout vectors, contiguous
    u1[i]: in    DATA_TYPE = i
    v1[j]: in    DATA_TYPE = j
    u2[i]: in    DATA_TYPE = i
    v2[j]: in    DATA_TYPE = j
    y[i]:  in    DATA_TYPE = i
    z[i]:  in    DATA_TYPE = i
    x[i]:  inout DATA_TYPE = i
    w[i]:  inout DATA_TYPE = i

    # Temporaries to reduce arithmetic and improve reuse
    # y_beta[j] = beta * y[j], reused across all i in x-update
    y_beta[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = j
    # x_alpha[j] = alpha * x[j], reused across all i in w-update
    x_alpha[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = j

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE
    # Tunable blocking and vectorization parameters
    TI: int  # tile size for i
    TJ: int  # tile size for j
    VEC: int # SIMD width in elements (e.g., 4 or 8)

computation:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1) Rank-2 update:
    #    A <- A + u1 * v1^T + u2 * v2^T
    #    Matches:
    #      for i
    #        for j
    #          A[i][j] += u1[i]*v1[j] + u2[i]*v2[j];
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    A_UPDATE:
      for i, j:
        A[i, j] = A[i, j]
                  + u1[i] * v1[j]
                  + u2[i] * v2[j]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2a) Precompute beta-scaled y to avoid recomputing beta*y[j]
    #     in the matrix–vector product.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    Y_SCALE:
      for j in [0, N):
        y_beta[j] = beta * y[j]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2b) x <- x + beta * A^T * y
    #     Implemented as:
    #       x[i] = x[i] + sum_j A[j, i] * y_beta[j]
    #     Matches:
    #       for i
    #         for j
    #           x[i] += beta * A[j][i] * y[j];
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    X_UPDATE:
      for i in [0, N):
        x[i] = x[i] + sum(j in [0, N), A[j, i] * y_beta[j])

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3) x <- x + z   and   x_alpha <- alpha * x
    #    We fuse the add and scale so alpha*x[j] is computed once and
    #    reused in the next matrix–vector product.
    #    Matches:
    #      for i
    #        x[i] += z[i];
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    X_ADD_Z_AND_SCALE:
      for i in [0, N):
        x[i]      = x[i] + z[i]
        x_alpha[i] = alpha * x[i]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4) w <- w + alpha * A * x
    #    Implemented as:
    #      w[i] = w[i] + sum_j A[i, j] * x_alpha[j]
    #    Matches:
    #      for i
    #        for j
    #          w[i] += alpha * A[i][j] * x[j];
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    W_UPDATE:
      for i in [0, N):
        w[i] = w[i] + sum(j in [0, N), A[i, j] * x_alpha[j])

dependencies:
    # Global phase ordering (barriers between phases)
    A_UPDATE -> Y_SCALE -> X_UPDATE -> X_ADD_Z_AND_SCALE -> W_UPDATE

optimization:
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # General notes:
    # - A is row-major. Loops that iterate j as the innermost index
    #   over A[i, j] benefit from unit-stride accesses.
    # - y_beta and x_alpha eliminate one multiplication per A-access
    #   in X_UPDATE and W_UPDATE, cutting total multiplications from
    #   ~6 N^2 to ~4 N^2.
    # - Parallelization is across i (or i-tiles), since updates to
    #   distinct elements of x[i] and w[i] are independent.
    # --------------------------------------------------------------

    # ---------------- A_UPDATE: rank-2 update of A -----------------
    # Tile the i and j loops so that an A tile plus the needed u/v
    # slices fit in cache.
    block(i, I_A, TI)
    block(j, J_A, TJ)
    hoist(I_A)              # make tile loops outermost

    # Parallelize across i-tiles; each tile writes disjoint rows of A.
    parallelize(I_A)

    # Vectorize inner j over contiguous A[i, j], v1[j], v2[j].
    vectorize(j, VEC)

    # Optionally hoist row-invariant u1[i], u2[i] into registers
    hoist(i)   # keep u1[i], u2[i] in registers within the inner j-loop

    # ------------- X_UPDATE: x += A^T * (beta y) ------------------
    # Access pattern A[j, i] is column-wise in the naive loop nest;
    # to make it row-major, we compute the reduction sum over j using
    # a j-outer, i-inner implementation within tiles.
    #
    # Mathematically:
    #   x[i] = x[i] + sum_j A[j, i] * y_beta[j]
    # allows reordering of (i, j) iteration as long as the sum over j
    # for each x[i] is preserved.

    block(j, J_X, TJ)       # tile over rows of A
    block(i, I_X, TI)       # tile over columns of A
    interchange(i, j)       # implement tiles as:
                            #   for J_X
                            #     for I_X
                            #       for j in tile J_X
                            #         for i in tile I_X:
                            #           x[i] += A[j, i] * y_beta[j]

    # Parallelize across I_X tiles: each x[i] is updated independently.
    parallelize(I_X)

    # Vectorize across i inside a fixed row j to exploit unit-stride
    # accesses to A[j, i] and x[i].
    vectorize(i, VEC)

    # ------------- X_ADD_Z_AND_SCALE: x += z; x_alpha = alpha*x ---
    # Simple 1D loop; trivially parallel and vectorizable.
    parallelize(i)
    vectorize(i, VEC)

    # ------------- W_UPDATE: w += A * (alpha x) -------------------
    # Standard GEMV with row-major A: i-outer, j-inner is already
    # cache-friendly and vectorizable.

    block(i, I_W, TI)
    block(j, J_W, TJ)
    hoist(I_W)              # outer tile in i

    # Parallelize across I_W tiles: each tile updates disjoint w[i].
    parallelize(I_W)

    # Vectorize across inner j over contiguous A[i, j], x_alpha[j].
    vectorize(j, VEC)

    # ----------------- Optional higher-level tweak ----------------
    # fuse(A_UPDATE, X_UPDATE):
    #   # Conceptual directive (not standard):
    #   # Evaluate A_UPDATE and X_UPDATE in a single (i, j) traversal:
    #   #   - First update A[i, j] using u1[i], v1[j], u2[i], v2[j].
    #   #   - Immediately accumulate into x[j] using y_beta[i] and the
    #   #     updated A[i, j]:
    #   #       x[j] += A[i, j] * y_beta[i]
    #   # This preserves x = x + beta * A^T * y mathematically while
    #   # reducing A traffic from two passes (update, then A^T*y) to one.
--- END OF MODEL: gemver-01 ---

--- START OF MODEL: gemver-02 ---
domain:
    # Problem size (square matrix)
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # Matrix A is stored row-major: A[i, j] at offset i * N + j
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Input vectors (read-only inside the kernel)
    u1[i]: in DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    u2[i]: in DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    v1[j]: in DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    v2[j]: in DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    y[j]:  in DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    z[i]:  in DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i

    # Input/output vectors (updated in the kernel)
    x[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    w[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i

    # Temporaries introduced for optimization
    # y_beta holds β * y, to avoid multiplying by β inside the N×N loop
    y_beta[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    # x_alpha holds α * x after x has been updated, 
    # so α is not multiplied inside the N×N loop for w
    x_alpha[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j

parameters:
    N: index_type                 # matrix / vector size
    alpha: DATA_TYPE              # scalar α
    beta:  DATA_TYPE              # scalar β

    # Tunable blocking and vectorization parameters
    TI: index_type                # tile size for i (e.g., 64)
    TJ: index_type                # tile size for j (e.g., 64)
    TJ_x: index_type              # tile size for j in x-update (e.g., 256)
    VEC: index_type               # SIMD width in elements (e.g., 4 for double on AVX2)

computation:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Rank-1 updates:
    #    A := A + u1 * v1^T + u2 * v2^T
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    A_update:
        for i, j:
            A[i, j] = A[i, j] + u1[i] * v1[j] + u2[i] * v2[j]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Pre-scale y by β to reduce multiplications in the A^T * y phase:
    #    y_beta[j] = β * y[j]
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    scale_y:
        for j:
            y_beta[j] = beta * y[j]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Compute:
    #       x[i] := x[i] + β * (A^T y)[i] + z[i]
    #    using the pre-scaled y_beta:
    #       x[i] := x[i] + sum_j A[j, i] * y_beta[j] + z[i]
    #
    #    This fuses the original second and third loops while preserving
    #    the mathematical result for x.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    x_update:
        for i:
            x[i] = x[i] + sum(j, A[j, i] * y_beta[j]) + z[i]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Pre-scale x by α once, instead of multiplying by α inside the
    #    N×N loop for w:
    #       x_alpha[j] = α * x[j]
    #    This preserves the final x and w semantics:
    #       original: w := w + α * A * x
    #       now:      w := w + A * (α * x) = w + α * A * x
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    scale_x:
        for j:
            x_alpha[j] = alpha * x[j]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Final matrix-vector product:
    #       w[i] := w[i] + α * (A x)[i]
    #    implemented as:
    #       w[i] := w[i] + sum_j A[i, j] * x_alpha[j]
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    w_update:
        for i:
            w[i] = w[i] + sum(j, A[i, j] * x_alpha[j])

dependencies:
    # A must be fully updated before it is used in x_update and w_update
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):
        A_update(i, j) -> x_update(i)   # x_update(i) uses A[j, i] for all j
        A_update(i, j) -> w_update(i)   # w_update(i) uses A[i, j] for all j

    # scale_y must finish before x_update uses y_beta
    for i in [0, N):
        scale_y(*) -> x_update(i)

    # scale_x must finish before w_update uses x_alpha
    for i in [0, N):
        scale_x(*) -> w_update(i)

optimization:
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # General goals:
    #   - Improve cache locality via 2D blocking (tiling) on A.
    #   - Reduce scalar multiplications by hoisting α and β out of
    #     the N×N loops (done structurally via y_beta and x_alpha).
    #   - Exploit outer-loop parallelism across i-tiles and i-rows.
    #   - Vectorize inner loops over j where A is accessed contiguously.
    # --------------------------------------------------------------

    # 1) 2D blocking for loops that traverse A row-wise (A_update, w_update).
    #    This increases temporal locality in A and in the vectors v1, v2, x_alpha.
    block(i, Ii, TI)      # i = Ii * TI + ii
    block(j, Jj, TJ)      # j = Jj * TJ + jj
    hoist(Ii)             # move tile loops Ii, Jj outermost
    hoist(Jj)

    # 2) Additional 1D blocking for the j dimension in x_update's reduction.
    #    This improves reuse of y_beta[j] and keeps partial A columns in cache.
    block(j, Jx, TJ_x)

    # 3) Parallelism:
    #    - A_update: different rows (and tiles of rows) of A are independent.
    #    - scale_y, scale_x: each element is independent.
    #    - x_update: each x[i] is an independent reduction over j.
    #    - w_update: each w[i] is an independent reduction over j.
    #
    #    We therefore parallelize the outer i-like dimensions.
    parallelize(Ii)       # tile-parallelism for A_update and w_update
    parallelize(i)        # row-parallelism for x_update
    parallelize(j)        # element-parallelism for scale_y and scale_x

    # 4) Vectorization:
    #    - A[i, j] is contiguous in j (row-major), so vectorize j where
    #      A is accessed as A[i, j].
    #    - In x_update, the reduction is over j, so we also vectorize j.
    vectorize(j, VEC)     # encourage SIMD on inner j loops

    # 5) Unrolling:
    #    Unroll inner j loops moderately to reduce loop-control overhead
    #    and expose more ILP for the compiler and hardware.
    unroll(j, 4)

    # 6) Scalar hoisting:
    #    Although reflected structurally in the computation, conceptually:
    #      - Treat beta as hoisted into y_beta (one multiply per j).
    #      - Treat alpha as hoisted into x_alpha (one multiply per j).
    #    This removes multiplications by α and β from the O(N^2) loops.
    #    (No explicit directive needed beyond the temp arrays.)
--- END OF MODEL: gemver-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: gemver-03 ---
domain:
    # Single problem size N; all loops iterate over [0, N)
    i: dim in [0, N)          # generic row index
    j: dim in [0, N)          # generic column index

data:
    # Row-major N×N matrix A
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # row-major

    # Input vectors
    u1[i]: in  DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    u2[i]: in  DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    v1[j]: in  DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    v2[j]: in  DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
    y[i]:  in  DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    z[i]:  in  DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i

    # Output / temporary vectors
    x[i]:  temp DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i   # x is fully overwritten in the kernel
    w[i]:  out  DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i

    # Optional helper to reduce arithmetic in x computation:
    beta_y[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j   # stores beta * y[j]

parameters:
    N: int
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable blocking / SIMD parameters (chosen for target x64 machine).
    TI: int    # tile size in i-dimension (rows), e.g., 64
    TJ: int    # tile size in j-dimension (cols), e.g., 64
    VEC: int   # SIMD vector width along contiguous dimension (e.g., 8 for AVX2 doubles)

computation:
    # 1) Rank‑1 update: A := A + u1 v1ᵀ + u2 v2ᵀ
    UPDATE_A:
        for i, j:
            A[i, j] = A[i, j] + u1[i] * v1[j] + u2[i] * v2[j]

    # 2) x := beta * Aᵀ y + z
    #    The original code does:
    #      x[i] += beta * A[j][i] * y[j]   (double loop)
    #      x[i] += z[i]                    (single loop)
    #    with x initialized to 0.
    #    Mathematically: x[i] = z[i] + beta * sum_j A[j, i] * y[j].
    PRECOMPUTE_BETA_Y:
        for j:
            beta_y[j] = beta * y[j]

    COMPUTE_X:
        for i:
            x[i] = z[i] + sum(j, A[j, i] * beta_y[j])

    # 3) w := alpha * A x
    #    Original: w[i] += alpha * A[i][j] * x[j] with w initialized to 0,
    #    so w[i] = alpha * sum_j A[i, j] * x[j].
    COMPUTE_W:
        for i:
            w[i] = alpha * sum(j, A[i, j] * x[j])

dependencies:
    # A must be fully updated before it is used in x or w.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, N), i2 in [0, N):
        UPDATE_A(i, j) -> COMPUTE_X(i2)
        UPDATE_A(i, j) -> COMPUTE_W(i2)

    # x must be fully computed before it is used in w.
    for i in [0, N), i2 in [0, N):
        COMPUTE_X(i) -> COMPUTE_W(i2)

optimization:
    #-----------------------------------------
    # 1) Optimize UPDATE_A: A += u1 v1ᵀ + u2 v2ᵀ
    #-----------------------------------------
    UPDATE_A:
        # Block over rows and columns so that working tiles of A, v1, v2
        # stay in L1/L2 cache.
        block(i, I_A, TI)      # outer tile index I_A, tile size TI in i
        block(j, J_A, TJ)      # outer tile index J_A, tile size TJ in j

        # Parallelize across row tiles: each thread updates disjoint rows of A.
        parallelize(I_A)

        # Within a row, j is contiguous in memory (row-major), good for SIMD.
        vectorize(j, VEC)

        # Hoist per-row invariants out of the inner j-loop:
        #   t1 = u1[i]; t2 = u2[i];
        #   A[i, j] += t1 * v1[j] + t2 * v2[j];
        hoist(i)

    #-----------------------------------------
    # 2) Optimize COMPUTE_X: x = z + beta * Aᵀ y
    #-----------------------------------------
    PRECOMPUTE_BETA_Y:
        # Simple vector multiply; trivially vectorizable and parallelizable.
        parallelize(j)
        vectorize(j, VEC)

    COMPUTE_X:
        # Implement as a cache-friendly sweep over rows of A:
        #   for j in [0,N):
        #       t = beta_y[j]
        #       for i in [0,N):
        #           x[i] += A[j, i] * t
        # This is equivalent to the reduction formulation above and
        # converts the column access A[*, i] into contiguous row access A[j, *].
        interchange(i, j)   # j outer, i inner for this kernel

        # Vectorize inner loop over i; A[j, i] is contiguous in i after interchange.
        vectorize(i, VEC)

        # Optional parallelization over j requires treating x as a reduction:
        # each thread accumulates into a private x_local[i] and these are
        # summed at the end. This adds O(#threads * N) extra storage, which
        # remains well below the 50% memory overhead bound since A is O(N²).
        parallelize(j)

    #-----------------------------------------
    # 3) Optimize COMPUTE_W: w = alpha * A x
    #-----------------------------------------
    COMPUTE_W:
        # Use the natural row-major traversal: i outer, j inner.
        block(i, I_W, TI)      # reuse the same row blocking as in UPDATE_A
        parallelize(I_W)       # distribute row tiles across threads

        # j is contiguous in memory along each row of A.
        vectorize(j, VEC)

        # Hoist per-row invariant alpha and reuse x[j] loaded once per chunk.
        hoist(i)

    #-----------------------------------------
    # General notes:
    # - All reductions over j are expressed via sum(j, ...), enabling
    #   the compiler/runtime to implement them with thread-local
    #   accumulators plus a final combine step if parallelized.
    # - Extra memory:
    #     * beta_y[N] (one additional N-vector),
    #     * optional per-thread reduction buffers of size O(N),
    #   which keeps the total memory footprint within 50% of the original
    #   (dominated by the N×N matrix A).
--- END OF MODEL: gemver-03 ---
